source: PALS first-party authored, generic-OpenMath and Lean-verified candidate set
scope_note: Generic OpenMath has no type constructor for relations, functions, finite sets, or cardinal numbers. Relation cards are concrete integer-order instances; map cards use scalar equations or closed finite-set images; cardinality cards use only closed finite literals; pigeonhole cards are explicitly enumerated boxes rather than a general function theorem.

examples: R is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive on X
R is a partial order on X
typed_backlog.why_current_profile_cannot_represent_it: A bare generic term cannot be bound as a relation X × X → Prop, so relation properties cannot be linked to one carrier set.
The generic profile cannot bind a function together with coherent source and target sorts, nor state its universal mapping property.

typed_backlog.topic: general finite cardinality and binomial coefficients
typed_backlog.why_current_profile_cannot_represent_it: set1:size has no finite-set or natural-number dependent sort in the generic profile, and no supported binomial-coefficient symbol is registered.
It quantifies a typed function and compares linked finite cardinalities; the explicitly enumerated instances above avoid that unsupported abstraction.

validation_contract.generic_openmath: All cards run statement-semantics validation, current retrieval C14N, and exact C14N validation during generation.
validation_contract.lean: Pass --verify-lean to compile one temporary file containing every witness in the pinned Lean workspace.
validation_contract.local_db: Pass --verify-db --expected-db-count 253 to perform read-only ID and C14N collision checks against the local legacy Draft DB.

cards.proof_strategy: Count the union and intersection, then verify the closed inclusion-exclusion equation.
sketch_steps: setup: Write the finite sets and their distinct listed elements explicitly.
operation: Form the displayed union, intersection, difference, product, or image.
enumerate: Remove duplicate elements and list the resulting finite set.
count: Count its elements or compare the two explicit finite sets.
conclude: State the requested finite-set identity.
cards.lean_witness: example : (({1, 2} : Finset ℤ) ∪ {2, 3}).card + (({1, 2} : Finset ℤ) ∩ {2, 3}).card = ({1, 2} : Finset ℤ).card + ({2, 3} : Finset ℤ).card := by norm_num

cards.canonical_statement: For all integers a, b, c in {0,1}, either a = b, a = c, or b = c.

cards.proof_strategy: Exhaust the two possible boxes for each of the three integers.
sketch_steps: setup: Record that every listed integer lies in the displayed finite box set.
cases: Split each value into the finitely many allowed box labels.
compare: In every exhaustive branch, identify two equal labels.
conclude: Assemble the resulting disjunction of pair equalities.
cards.lean_witness:
example (a b c : ℤ) (ha : a = 0 ∨ a = 1) (hb : b = 0 ∨ b = 1) (hc : c = 0 ∨ c = 1) : a = b ∨ a = c ∨ b = c := by
  rcases ha with ha | ha <;> rcases hb with hb | hb <;> rcases hc with hc | hc <;> omega

cards.proof_strategy: Exhaust the three possible boxes for four integers and select a repeated label.
sketch_steps: setup: Record that every listed integer lies in the displayed finite box set.
cases: Split each value into the finitely many allowed box labels.
compare: In every exhaustive branch, identify two equal labels.
conclude: Assemble the resulting disjunction of pair equalities.
